pll1d20c1-d1e3477.summary: Announces that it remains to show that no person exceeds another in power, so that, as magnitude is one and undifferentiated, so is power.

pll1d20c1-d1e3480.summary: States that the Father is not more powerful than the Son, nor either than the Spirit, and that two or three together are not more powerful than one, since the Son received the Father's omnipotence by being born and the Spirit by proceeding. Augustine argues this against Maximinus, who held the Father more powerful and better than the Son.
claims: No person is more powerful than another.
Several persons together are not more powerful than one.
The Son and Spirit receive omnipotence through birth and procession.

pl-l1d20c1.summary: Turns to the third element of equality, power: as the magnitude of the three is one and undifferentiated, so is their power. The Father is not more powerful than the Son, nor either than the Spirit, nor do two or three together have more power than one, since the Son received the Father's omnipotence by being born and the Spirit by proceeding. Augustine argues this against Maximinus, who held the Father more powerful and better than the Son.
claims: The three persons have one and the same power.
No person is more powerful than another, and several together are not more powerful than one.
The Son received the Father's omnipotence by being born, the Spirit by proceeding.
